Among the wonders of Allah's creation is a vine-clustered one, some of its grapes greenish and others ghirabib.

﴿And among people, beasts, and livestock, their colors vary likewise.﴾ The historian said: the pronoun "alwanuhu" (its colors) is because of "min" (among). Ustadhi Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ayyash say: He said "alwanuhu" because it refers back to "ma" in the implied sense, meaning: among people, beasts, and livestock is that whose colors vary.

﴿Thus﴾: the sentence is complete here, meaning: among these things are those whose colors vary according to the variation of fruits. Then He began, saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.﴾ It is narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he recited (innama yakhsha Allahu) with Allah in the nominative and (al-'ulama') in the accusative, which was the choice of Abu Hanifa, meaning "Allah knows," and it was said: "chooses." The correct reading is that of the common people.

It was also said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us from Ishaq ibn Sadaqah, who said: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us from Sayf ibn Umar, who said: Abbas ibn Awsajah narrated to us from Ata' al-Khurasani, raising the hadith, who said: Fear appeared in Abu Bakr to the point that it was recognized in him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) spoke to him about that, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah﴾ concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). And in the hadith: "The most knowledgeable of them of Allah is the one most fearful of Him."

Masruq said: It is sufficient knowledge for a person that he fears Allah, and sufficient ignorance for a person that he is pleased with his knowledge.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Rabi'i narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Muharrami narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Malik al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'd narrated to us from Salih ibn Muslim al-Laythi, who said: A man came to al-Sha'bi and said: "Give me a fatwa, O scholar!" He said: "The scholar is one who fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty, Forgiving. Indeed those who recite the Book of Allah...﴾ The verse. Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: This is the verse of the reciters: ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: Ju'aywah narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr al-Laythi that he said: A man stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is it that I do not love death?" He said: "Do you have wealth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then send it forward." He said: "I cannot." He said: "Indeed, the heart of a person is with his wealth: if he sends it forward, he loves to be joined to it, and if he delays it, he loves to be delayed along with it."

﴿Hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾. Al-Farra' said: the phrase "yarjuna" (hoping) is the response to "inna alladhina yatlun" (indeed those who recite).

﴿That He may give them their full rewards and increase them from His bounty. Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it. Indeed Allah is, of His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing.﴾ "Thumma" is related back to what precedes it of the books of Allah in His words "limа bayna yadayhi" (what is before it), meaning the earlier books that preceded it; that is, We sent down those books. ﴿Then We caused to inherit this Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants.﴾ It is possible that "thumma" here means "wa" (and), meaning "and We caused to inherit," like His words: ﴿and then he was among those who believed﴾ [Surah al-Balad: 17], meaning "and he was." The meaning of "awrathna" is "We gave," because inheritance is a gift; this was said by Mujahid. Some of the people of meaning said: "awrathna" means "We delayed," and from it comes "mirath" (inheritance), because it comes after the deceased. Its meaning: We delayed the Qur'an relative to the earlier nations, and We gave it to you and qualified you for it. Antarah said:

And I bequeathed my sword from Husayn ibn Mu'aqqil, to his grandfather; indeed I am seeking my vengeance.

That is, I delayed it. In this is an honour for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), since He said "awrathna" to them, and said to the other nations: ﴿inherit the Book﴾, the verse, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He divided them into three classes and ranked them into three degrees, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾. He restricted the word and attached the wronging to the self, and therefore it is permissible that he be among those chosen despite his wronging.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in mentioning the wrongdoer first and delaying the foremost, when one normally mentions the more excellent first?

The answer to that is that we say: He delayed the foremost so that he would be nearer to the gardens and the reward, just as He mentioned the monasteries, churches and prayers in Surat al-Hajj before the mosques, which are the most excellent places on earth, so that the monasteries would be nearer to destruction and ruin, and the mosques nearer to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.

Some said: this was done because when kings wish to combine things in mention, they put the lesser before the greater, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 6], and He said: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 61], and He said: ﴿He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 49], and He said: ﴿He who created death and life﴾ [Surah al-Mulk: 2].

It was also said: He put the wrongdoer first so that he would not despair of His mercy, and delayed the foremost so that he would not be conceited about his deed.

Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "He began with the wrongdoer to inform that one draws near to Him only through the turning of His mercy and generosity, and that wronging does not affect the state of being chosen. Then He followed with the moderate, because they are between fear and hope, then He concluded with the foremost, so that no one would feel safe from the plotting of Allah, and they are all in Paradise by the sanctity of the word of sincerity."

Some of them said: He put the wrongdoer first because he had nothing to rely upon except the mercy of Allah, so he relied upon Allah and depended upon His mercy; the moderate relied upon his good opinion of his Lord; and the foremost relied upon his good deeds and obedience.

Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them in being chosen to remove objections regarding the bestowal, because being chosen necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitating being chosen. Therefore it was said: "Establish the lineage correctly, then hope for the inheritance."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He arranged them in this order according to the stations of people, because the states of a servant are three: disobedience, heedlessness, then repentance and nearness. When he disobeys, he enters the domain of the wrongdoers; when he repents, he enters the group of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are abundant, he is connected to Allah and enters the ranks of the foremost.

The exegetes and interpreters differed about the meaning of the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost, and they went on at length. I will mention the texts of what they said, and success is from Allah:

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Burhan ibn Ali al-Sufi and al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab informed me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us from al-A'mash from Abu Thabit that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my strangeness, comfort my loneliness, and grant me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, I am happier with that than you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah,﴾ and he said:

"As for the foremost, he will enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be held in the place of standing, then he will enter Paradise. They are the ones who said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Kindi and al-A'mash said from a man from Abu Thabit. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qatee'i informed me from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal: my father narrated to me from Ishaq ibn Isa, who narrated to me from Anas ibn Iyad al-Laythi Abu Damrah, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah.﴾ As for those who were foremost in good deeds, they are those who enter Paradise without reckoning. As for those who were moderate, they will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they are the ones who will be kept long in the place of gathering; then they are the ones whom Allah receives with His mercy, and they are the ones who say: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Sam'an al-Dharrar narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri' at Wasit narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: Faraj ibn Fudalah narrated to us from Azhar ibn Abd Allah al-Harrazi, who said: One who heard Uthman ibn Affan narrated to me that he recited this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants,﴾ the verse, and said: "Our foremost are the people of our jihad, our moderate are the people of our settled regions, and our wrongdoers are the people of our desert."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us from al-Salt ibn Dinar, saying: Uqbah ibn Sahban narrated to us, saying: I entered upon Aisha and asked her about the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; among them is one who wrongs himself...﴾ She said to me: "My son, they are all in Paradise. As for the foremost in good deeds, they are those who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bore witness of Paradise. As for the moderate, they are those who followed his path among his companions until they joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and you." Thus she placed herself with us.

Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: they said they are the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah) ... ; ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾: they are the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah) ...; ﴿and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾: they are the foremost, the drawn near (al-muqarrabun), among all people.

Qatadah said: This is in the world, in three stations; and at death Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right... and the burning of Hell﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 90–94], and in the Hereafter also, He the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And you will be three groups. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right! ... the drawn near﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 7–11].

Ibn Abbas said: The foremost is the sincere believer, the moderate is the showy one, and the wrongdoer is the one ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, though not denying them, because He judged for all three the entry into Paradise, saying: ﴿gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾. I heard Abu Muhammad Shaybah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abd say: Aisha said:

The foremost: the one who embraced Islam before the Hijrah; the moderate: the one who embraced Islam after the Hijrah; and the wrongdoer: we.

Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati said: The one who wrongs himself is the one who died upon a major sin without repenting from it; the moderate is the one who did not commit a major sin; and the foremost in good deeds is the one who never disobeyed Allah, and the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.

From al-Hasan also, he said: The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds; the moderate is the one whose good and evil deeds are equal; and the wrongdoer is the one whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: The foremost is the scholar, the moderate is the student, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant. And from him also: The foremost is the one occupied with his afterlife; the moderate is the one occupied with his afterlife rather than his livelihood; and the wrongdoer is the one occupied with his livelihood rather than his afterlife.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the seeker of this world, the moderate is the seeker of the final abode, and the foremost is the seeker of the Lord.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the Muslim, the moderate is the believer, and the foremost is the doer of good.

And they said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: ... (no, continue below)

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given. Here is the translation:

And it was said: "The wrongdoer (al-zalim) is the one who shows off (yura'i) in all his deeds; the moderate (al-muqtasid) is the one whose deeds are partly for show and partly sincere; and the foremost (al-sabiq) is the one who is sincere in all his deeds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who takes the world, whether lawful or unlawful; the moderate is the one who strives to seek what is lawful; and the foremost is the one who has abandoned the world entirely and turned away from it."

Abu 'Uthman al-Hiri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who knows Allah with his tongue but whose deeds do not agree with his words; the moderate is the one who knows Him with his tongue and obeys Him with his limbs; and the foremost is the one who knows Him with his tongue, obeys Him with his limbs, and is sincere in his work." It was also said: "The foremost are the first emigrants (al-muhajirun al-awwalun), the moderate are the general body of the Companions, and the wrongdoers are the Successors (al-tabi'un)."

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz in Egypt say: Ibn 'Ata said: "The wrongdoer is the one whom you love for the sake of this world; the moderate is the one whom you love for the sake of the Hereafter; and the foremost is the one who lets his own desire fall before the desire of the Truth, so he sees no seeking or wanting for himself, because the authority of the Truth has overwhelmed him." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one whose outward appearance is better than his inward; the moderate is the one whose outward and inward are equal; and the foremost is the one whose inward is better than his outward."

It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah out of fear of the Fire; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of hope for Paradise; and the foremost is the one who worships Him without any cause." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the ascetic (al-zahid), the moderate is the knower (al-'arif), and the foremost is the lover (al-muhibb)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who despairs at affliction; the moderate is the one who is patient at affliction; and the foremost is the one who delights in affliction." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Him out of heedlessness and habit; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and dread; and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe and sight of the favour." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is given and then withholds; the moderate is the one who is given and then gives; and the foremost is the one who is withheld from and then gives thanks." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the heedless; the moderate is the seeker; and the foremost is the one who finds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is self-sufficient through his wealth; the moderate is the one who is self-sufficient through his religion; and the foremost is the one who is self-sufficient through his Lord." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the reciter of the Qur'an; the moderate is the reciter and the scholar of it; and the foremost is the reciter of the Book of Allah, the scholar of the Book of Allah, and the one who acts upon it." It was also said: "The foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the call to prayer (adhan); the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the adhan has been called; and the wrongdoer is the one who enters the mosque after the iqamah has been given." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who loves himself; the moderate is the one who loves his Lord; and the foremost is the one whom his Lord loves." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who seeks; the moderate is one who is sought; and the foremost is one who is brought near (maqrub)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who is called; the moderate is one who is given permission; and the foremost is one who is brought near." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is 'afuf; the moderate is alluf; and the foremost is halif."

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: "The wrongdoer seeks justice but does not grant it; the moderate grants justice and seeks it; and the foremost grants justice but does not seek it."

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who does not mention Allah with his tongue; the moderate is the one who mentions Him with his heart; and the foremost is the one who does not forget his Lord."

Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Antaki said: "The wrongdoer is the owner of words; the moderate is the owner of deeds; and the foremost is the owner of states."

Then Allah, glory be to Him, gathered them together in entering Paradise, and He said, glory be to Him: "Gardens of Eden, which they will enter."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Zur'a told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Asim al-Razi told us, saying: Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, known as al-Shadhakuni, told us, from Husayn ibn Numayr Abu Muhsin, from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother, from his father, from Usama ibn Zayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning: "Then of them is one who wrongs himself" — the verse — he said: "All of them are in Paradise." [57]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Fa'fa' al-Qadi told us, saying: Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi told us, saying: Abu Qilaba told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Husayn told us, from al-Fadl ibn 'Umayra, from Maymun al-Kurdi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Hindi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recite on the pulpit: "Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose of Our servants" — the verse — and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Our foremost is a foremost, our moderate is one who is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." [58] Abu Qilaba said: I related this to Yahya ibn Ma'in, and he began to marvel at it.

"They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bashir told us, saying: Abu al-Harith Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Umm Sa'id told us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi told us, saying: Usayd ibn Musa told us, from Ibn Thawman, from 'Ata' ibn Qurra, from 'Abd Allah ibn Damra, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the lowest of the people of Paradise's adornment were weighed against the adornment of all the people of this world, the adornment with which Allah adorns him in the Hereafter would be better than the adornment of all the people of this world." [59]

"And they will say," i.e., they will say when they enter Paradise: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us." Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-'Adl informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Hammad al-Baghdadi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas told us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham told me, from my father, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Ibn Abi al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: "The grief of the Fire."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi, who said: Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani told us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Dawud al-Harrani told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Ash'ath ibn Qays, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyya concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: "The grief of bread."

'Ikrima: the grief of sins and misdeeds and the fear that obedience will be rejected. It was also said: the grief of death. It was also said: the grief of not knowing whether one will go to Paradise or Hell. al-Thumali: the grief of this world. al-Dahhak: the grief of Iblis and his whisperings.

Dhu al-Nun: the grief of separation.

al-Kalbi: meaning the grief that saddens us in this world about the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the grief of punishment and reckoning. It was also said: the grief of the horrors and terrors of this world. al-Qasim said: the grief of the loss of blessings, the turning of the heart, and the fear of the outcome.

I heard al-Sulami say: I heard al-Nasrabadhi say: Their grief was only the management of their affairs and the governance of their souls; so when they were saved from it, they praised Allah, and they said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us. Indeed our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative."

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi, from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "There is no loneliness upon the people of 'there is no god but Allah' in their graves, nor at their gathering, nor at their dispersal. As if I see the people of 'there is no god but Allah' coming out of their graves, shaking the dust from their faces, and saying: 'Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us. Indeed our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative.'" [60]

"Who has settled us in the abode of permanence (al-muqama), by His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein." That is, the settlement (al-iqama). "Nasab" (fatigue) means exhaustion, weariness and lassitude. The common reading has the lam with a damma (lughub), while al-Sulami read it with a fatha (lughab), which is also a verbal noun, like wulu' (ardour). al-Farra' said: it is as if he made it like what causes exhaustion (yulghab), similar to lughub.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juzqani informed us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn Muhammadawayh [sic in the original] the righteous man, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Kharazmi, who said: 'Asim ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: Isma'il told me, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim concerning the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: When the people of Paradise enter, the young servants and attendants meet them, as if they were hidden pearls. He said: Then Allah sends an angel from among the angels, with a gift from the Lord of the worlds and a garment from the garments of Paradise, and he clothes him. He said: Then he wishes to enter Paradise, and the angel says: "Stay as you are," and he stops, and with him are ten rings from the rings of Paradise, a gift from the Lord of the worlds, and he places them on his fingers. Written on the first ring: "Enter it, abiding forever" [Q. 39:73]; and on the second, written: "Enter it in peace; that is the day of abiding" [Q. 50:34]; and on the third, written: "Your griefs and cares have been lifted"; and on the fourth, written: "We have married you to the wide-eyed houris"; and on the fifth, written: "Enter it in peace, secure"; and on the sixth, written: "Indeed I have rewarded them today for what they endured" [Q. 23:111]; and on the seventh, written: "That they are the successful"; and on the eighth: "You have become secure, you will not fear"; and on the ninth, written: "You have been made companions of the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs"; and on the tenth, written: "You have dwelt in the neighbourhood of One who does not harm neighbours." Then the angels say: "Enter it in peace, secure."

"When they entered houses raised up, they said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us...' to His saying: 'fatigue.'"

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 35, verse 15–35 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. That is not difficult for Allah.﴾ ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl was asked about reconciling this verse with the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 13]. He said: ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ refers to bearing it willingly, while ﴿they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ refers to bearing it unwillingly.

﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative﴾, meaning: if a soul burdened with the sins of others calls [someone] to carry its load, that is, the load of the sins upon it, nothing of it will be carried, even if the one called were a relative: his son, his mother, his father, or his brother.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Razmah al-Qazwini narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abd ibn Amir al-Samarqandi, who said: Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Fudayl ibn Iyad say regarding the words of the Exalted, ﴿nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative﴾: The mother will meet her son on the Day of Resurrection and say: "My son, did not my belly serve as a vessel for you? Did not my breast provide you with drink?" He will say: "Yes, O mother." She will say: "My son, my sins have weighed me down, so carry one sin of mine for me." He will say: "O mother, leave me alone, for today I am preoccupied with myself."

﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, that is, who fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿and establish the prayer. Whoever purifies himself, purifies only for his own soul. And to Allah is the final return.﴾ "Purifies himself" means one who does good and righteous deeds. 

﴿The blind and the seeing are not alike﴾, meaning: the ignorant and the knowledgeable; ﴿nor are darknesses and light﴾, meaning: disbelief and faith; ﴿nor shade and scorching heat﴾, meaning: Paradise and Hellfire. Al-harur is the hot wind by night and the simoom by day. Some said: al-harur is the heat with the sun during the day. ﴿Nor are the living and the dead alike﴾, meaning: the believers and the disbelievers. ﴿Indeed Allah causes to hear whom He wills﴾, until he takes admonition and responds, ﴿but you cannot make hear those in the graves﴾, meaning: the disbelievers, whom He likened to the dead. Ashhab al-Uqayli recited (bi-musmi'i man fi al-qubur) without tanwin, as an idafah (construct).

﴿You are only a warner. Indeed We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them. And if they deny you, those before them had denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs and written scriptures and the illuminating Book.﴾ He repeated them, though they are one thing, because the wordings differ.

﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My rejection!﴾

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors?﴾ The adjective was placed before the noun, and therefore it is in the accusative. ﴿And among the mountains are tracts, white and red, of varying shades, and extremely black.﴾ Judad means paths; its singular is jaddah, like mudda and mudad. The plural of jadid is judud (with a damma on the dal), like sarir and surar. Al-Farra' said: there is inversion in it; its meaning is "black ghiraab," and ghirabib is the plural of gharib, meaning intensely black, likened to the color of a crow. A poet, describing a vineyard, said:

Among the wonders of Allah's creation is a vine-clustered one, some of its grapes greenish and others ghirabib.

﴿And among people, beasts, and livestock, their colors vary likewise.﴾ The historian said: the pronoun "alwanuhu" (its colors) is because of "min" (among). Ustadhi Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ayyash say: He said "alwanuhu" because it refers back to "ma" in the implied sense, meaning: among people, beasts, and livestock is that whose colors vary.

﴿Thus﴾: the sentence is complete here, meaning: among these things are those whose colors vary according to the variation of fruits. Then He began, saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.﴾ It is narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he recited (innama yakhsha Allahu) with Allah in the nominative and (al-'ulama') in the accusative, which was the choice of Abu Hanifa, meaning "Allah knows," and it was said: "chooses." The correct reading is that of the common people.

It was also said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us from Ishaq ibn Sadaqah, who said: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us from Sayf ibn Umar, who said: Abbas ibn Awsajah narrated to us from Ata' al-Khurasani, raising the hadith, who said: Fear appeared in Abu Bakr to the point that it was recognized in him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) spoke to him about that, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah﴾ concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). And in the hadith: "The most knowledgeable of them of Allah is the one most fearful of Him."

Masruq said: It is sufficient knowledge for a person that he fears Allah, and sufficient ignorance for a person that he is pleased with his knowledge.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Rabi'i narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Muharrami narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Malik al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'd narrated to us from Salih ibn Muslim al-Laythi, who said: A man came to al-Sha'bi and said: "Give me a fatwa, O scholar!" He said: "The scholar is one who fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty, Forgiving. Indeed those who recite the Book of Allah...﴾ The verse. Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: This is the verse of the reciters: ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: Ju'aywah narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr al-Laythi that he said: A man stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is it that I do not love death?" He said: "Do you have wealth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then send it forward." He said: "I cannot." He said: "Indeed, the heart of a person is with his wealth: if he sends it forward, he loves to be joined to it, and if he delays it, he loves to be delayed along with it."

﴿Hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾. Al-Farra' said: the phrase "yarjuna" (hoping) is the response to "inna alladhina yatlun" (indeed those who recite).

﴿That He may give them their full rewards and increase them from His bounty. Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it. Indeed Allah is, of His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing.﴾ "Thumma" is related back to what precedes it of the books of Allah in His words "limа bayna yadayhi" (what is before it), meaning the earlier books that preceded it; that is, We sent down those books. ﴿Then We caused to inherit this Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants.﴾ It is possible that "thumma" here means "wa" (and), meaning "and We caused to inherit," like His words: ﴿and then he was among those who believed﴾ [Surah al-Balad: 17], meaning "and he was." The meaning of "awrathna" is "We gave," because inheritance is a gift; this was said by Mujahid. Some of the people of meaning said: "awrathna" means "We delayed," and from it comes "mirath" (inheritance), because it comes after the deceased. Its meaning: We delayed the Qur'an relative to the earlier nations, and We gave it to you and qualified you for it. Antarah said:

And I bequeathed my sword from Husayn ibn Mu'aqqil, to his grandfather; indeed I am seeking my vengeance.

That is, I delayed it. In this is an honour for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), since He said "awrathna" to them, and said to the other nations: ﴿inherit the Book﴾, the verse, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He divided them into three classes and ranked them into three degrees, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾. He restricted the word and attached the wronging to the self, and therefore it is permissible that he be among those chosen despite his wronging.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in mentioning the wrongdoer first and delaying the foremost, when one normally mentions the more excellent first?

The answer to that is that we say: He delayed the foremost so that he would be nearer to the gardens and the reward, just as He mentioned the monasteries, churches and prayers in Surat al-Hajj before the mosques, which are the most excellent places on earth, so that the monasteries would be nearer to destruction and ruin, and the mosques nearer to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.

Some said: this was done because when kings wish to combine things in mention, they put the lesser before the greater, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 6], and He said: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 61], and He said: ﴿He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 49], and He said: ﴿He who created death and life﴾ [Surah al-Mulk: 2].

It was also said: He put the wrongdoer first so that he would not despair of His mercy, and delayed the foremost so that he would not be conceited about his deed.

Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "He began with the wrongdoer to inform that one draws near to Him only through the turning of His mercy and generosity, and that wronging does not affect the state of being chosen. Then He followed with the moderate, because they are between fear and hope, then He concluded with the foremost, so that no one would feel safe from the plotting of Allah, and they are all in Paradise by the sanctity of the word of sincerity."

Some of them said: He put the wrongdoer first because he had nothing to rely upon except the mercy of Allah, so he relied upon Allah and depended upon His mercy; the moderate relied upon his good opinion of his Lord; and the foremost relied upon his good deeds and obedience.

Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them in being chosen to remove objections regarding the bestowal, because being chosen necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitating being chosen. Therefore it was said: "Establish the lineage correctly, then hope for the inheritance."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He arranged them in this order according to the stations of people, because the states of a servant are three: disobedience, heedlessness, then repentance and nearness. When he disobeys, he enters the domain of the wrongdoers; when he repents, he enters the group of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are abundant, he is connected to Allah and enters the ranks of the foremost.

The exegetes and interpreters differed about the meaning of the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost, and they went on at length. I will mention the texts of what they said, and success is from Allah:

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Burhan ibn Ali al-Sufi and al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab informed me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us from al-A'mash from Abu Thabit that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my strangeness, comfort my loneliness, and grant me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, I am happier with that than you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah,﴾ and he said:

"As for the foremost, he will enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be held in the place of standing, then he will enter Paradise. They are the ones who said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Kindi and al-A'mash said from a man from Abu Thabit. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qatee'i informed me from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal: my father narrated to me from Ishaq ibn Isa, who narrated to me from Anas ibn Iyad al-Laythi Abu Damrah, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah.﴾ As for those who were foremost in good deeds, they are those who enter Paradise without reckoning. As for those who were moderate, they will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they are the ones who will be kept long in the place of gathering; then they are the ones whom Allah receives with His mercy, and they are the ones who say: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Sam'an al-Dharrar narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri' at Wasit narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: Faraj ibn Fudalah narrated to us from Azhar ibn Abd Allah al-Harrazi, who said: One who heard Uthman ibn Affan narrated to me that he recited this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants,﴾ the verse, and said: "Our foremost are the people of our jihad, our moderate are the people of our settled regions, and our wrongdoers are the people of our desert."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us from al-Salt ibn Dinar, saying: Uqbah ibn Sahban narrated to us, saying: I entered upon Aisha and asked her about the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; among them is one who wrongs himself...﴾ She said to me: "My son, they are all in Paradise. As for the foremost in good deeds, they are those who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bore witness of Paradise. As for the moderate, they are those who followed his path among his companions until they joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and you." Thus she placed herself with us.

Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: they said they are the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah) ... ; ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾: they are the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah) ...; ﴿and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾: they are the foremost, the drawn near (al-muqarrabun), among all people.

Qatadah said: This is in the world, in three stations; and at death Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right... and the burning of Hell﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 90–94], and in the Hereafter also, He the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And you will be three groups. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right! ... the drawn near﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 7–11].

Ibn Abbas said: The foremost is the sincere believer, the moderate is the showy one, and the wrongdoer is the one ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, though not denying them, because He judged for all three the entry into Paradise, saying: ﴿gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾. I heard Abu Muhammad Shaybah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abd say: Aisha said:

The foremost: the one who embraced Islam before the Hijrah; the moderate: the one who embraced Islam after the Hijrah; and the wrongdoer: we.

Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati said: The one who wrongs himself is the one who died upon a major sin without repenting from it; the moderate is the one who did not commit a major sin; and the foremost in good deeds is the one who never disobeyed Allah, and the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.

From al-Hasan also, he said: The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds; the moderate is the one whose good and evil deeds are equal; and the wrongdoer is the one whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: The foremost is the scholar, the moderate is the student, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant. And from him also: The foremost is the one occupied with his afterlife; the moderate is the one occupied with his afterlife rather than his livelihood; and the wrongdoer is the one occupied with his livelihood rather than his afterlife.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the seeker of this world, the moderate is the seeker of the final abode, and the foremost is the seeker of the Lord.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the Muslim, the moderate is the believer, and the foremost is the doer of good.

And they said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: ... (no, continue below)

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given. Here is the translation:

And it was said: "The wrongdoer (al-zalim) is the one who shows off (yura'i) in all his deeds; the moderate (al-muqtasid) is the one whose deeds are partly for show and partly sincere; and the foremost (al-sabiq) is the one who is sincere in all his deeds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who takes the world, whether lawful or unlawful; the moderate is the one who strives to seek what is lawful; and the foremost is the one who has abandoned the world entirely and turned away from it."

Abu 'Uthman al-Hiri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who knows Allah with his tongue but whose deeds do not agree with his words; the moderate is the one who knows Him with his tongue and obeys Him with his limbs; and the foremost is the one who knows Him with his tongue, obeys Him with his limbs, and is sincere in his work." It was also said: "The foremost are the first emigrants (al-muhajirun al-awwalun), the moderate are the general body of the Companions, and the wrongdoers are the Successors (al-tabi'un)."

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz in Egypt say: Ibn 'Ata said: "The wrongdoer is the one whom you love for the sake of this world; the moderate is the one whom you love for the sake of the Hereafter; and the foremost is the one who lets his own desire fall before the desire of the Truth, so he sees no seeking or wanting for himself, because the authority of the Truth has overwhelmed him." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one whose outward appearance is better than his inward; the moderate is the one whose outward and inward are equal; and the foremost is the one whose inward is better than his outward."

It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah out of fear of the Fire; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of hope for Paradise; and the foremost is the one who worships Him without any cause." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the ascetic (al-zahid), the moderate is the knower (al-'arif), and the foremost is the lover (al-muhibb)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who despairs at affliction; the moderate is the one who is patient at affliction; and the foremost is the one who delights in affliction." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Him out of heedlessness and habit; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and dread; and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe and sight of the favour." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is given and then withholds; the moderate is the one who is given and then gives; and the foremost is the one who is withheld from and then gives thanks." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the heedless; the moderate is the seeker; and the foremost is the one who finds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is self-sufficient through his wealth; the moderate is the one who is self-sufficient through his religion; and the foremost is the one who is self-sufficient through his Lord." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the reciter of the Qur'an; the moderate is the reciter and the scholar of it; and the foremost is the reciter of the Book of Allah, the scholar of the Book of Allah, and the one who acts upon it." It was also said: "The foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the call to prayer (adhan); the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the adhan has been called; and the wrongdoer is the one who enters the mosque after the iqamah has been given." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who loves himself; the moderate is the one who loves his Lord; and the foremost is the one whom his Lord loves." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who seeks; the moderate is one who is sought; and the foremost is one who is brought near (maqrub)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who is called; the moderate is one who is given permission; and the foremost is one who is brought near." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is 'afuf; the moderate is alluf; and the foremost is halif."

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: "The wrongdoer seeks justice but does not grant it; the moderate grants justice and seeks it; and the foremost grants justice but does not seek it."

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who does not mention Allah with his tongue; the moderate is the one who mentions Him with his heart; and the foremost is the one who does not forget his Lord."

Ahmad ibn 'Asim al-Antaki said: "The wrongdoer is the owner of words; the moderate is the owner of deeds; and the foremost is the owner of states."

Then Allah, glory be to Him, gathered them together in entering Paradise, and He said, glory be to Him: "Gardens of Eden, which they will enter."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Zur'a told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Asim al-Razi told us, saying: Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, known as al-Shadhakuni, told us, from Husayn ibn Numayr Abu Muhsin, from Ibn Abi Layla, from his brother, from his father, from Usama ibn Zayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning: "Then of them is one who wrongs himself" — the verse — he said: "All of them are in Paradise." [57]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Fa'fa' al-Qadi told us, saying: Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi told us, saying: Abu Qilaba told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Husayn told us, from al-Fadl ibn 'Umayra, from Maymun al-Kurdi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Hindi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recite on the pulpit: "Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose of Our servants" — the verse — and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Our foremost is a foremost, our moderate is one who is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." [58] Abu Qilaba said: I related this to Yahya ibn Ma'in, and he began to marvel at it.

"They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bashir told us, saying: Abu al-Harith Ahmad ibn Sa'id ibn Umm Sa'id told us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi told us, saying: Usayd ibn Musa told us, from Ibn Thawman, from 'Ata' ibn Qurra, from 'Abd Allah ibn Damra, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the lowest of the people of Paradise's adornment were weighed against the adornment of all the people of this world, the adornment with which Allah adorns him in the Hereafter would be better than the adornment of all the people of this world." [59]

"And they will say," i.e., they will say when they enter Paradise: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us." Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-'Adl informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn Hammad al-Baghdadi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas told us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham told me, from my father, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Ibn Abi al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: "The grief of the Fire."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi, who said: Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani told us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Dawud al-Harrani told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Ash'ath ibn Qays, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyya concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: "The grief of bread."

'Ikrima: the grief of sins and misdeeds and the fear that obedience will be rejected. It was also said: the grief of death. It was also said: the grief of not knowing whether one will go to Paradise or Hell. al-Thumali: the grief of this world. al-Dahhak: the grief of Iblis and his whisperings.

Dhu al-Nun: the grief of separation.

al-Kalbi: meaning the grief that saddens us in this world about the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the grief of punishment and reckoning. It was also said: the grief of the horrors and terrors of this world. al-Qasim said: the grief of the loss of blessings, the turning of the heart, and the fear of the outcome.

I heard al-Sulami say: I heard al-Nasrabadhi say: Their grief was only the management of their affairs and the governance of their souls; so when they were saved from it, they praised Allah, and they said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us. Indeed our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative."

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi, from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "There is no loneliness upon the people of 'there is no god but Allah' in their graves, nor at their gathering, nor at their dispersal. As if I see the people of 'there is no god but Allah' coming out of their graves, shaking the dust from their faces, and saying: 'Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us. Indeed our Lord is Most Forgiving, Most Appreciative.'" [60]

"Who has settled us in the abode of permanence (al-muqama), by His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein." That is, the settlement (al-iqama). "Nasab" (fatigue) means exhaustion, weariness and lassitude. The common reading has the lam with a damma (lughub), while al-Sulami read it with a fatha (lughab), which is also a verbal noun, like wulu' (ardour). al-Farra' said: it is as if he made it like what causes exhaustion (yulghab), similar to lughub.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juzqani informed us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahdi informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn Muhammadawayh [sic in the original] the righteous man, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Kharazmi, who said: 'Asim ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: Isma'il told me, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim concerning the saying of Allah, glory be to Him: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us," who said: When the people of Paradise enter, the young servants and attendants meet them, as if they were hidden pearls. He said: Then Allah sends an angel from among the angels, with a gift from the Lord of the worlds and a garment from the garments of Paradise, and he clothes him. He said: Then he wishes to enter Paradise, and the angel says: "Stay as you are," and he stops, and with him are ten rings from the rings of Paradise, a gift from the Lord of the worlds, and he places them on his fingers. Written on the first ring: "Enter it, abiding forever" [Q. 39:73]; and on the second, written: "Enter it in peace; that is the day of abiding" [Q. 50:34]; and on the third, written: "Your griefs and cares have been lifted"; and on the fourth, written: "We have married you to the wide-eyed houris"; and on the fifth, written: "Enter it in peace, secure"; and on the sixth, written: "Indeed I have rewarded them today for what they endured" [Q. 23:111]; and on the seventh, written: "That they are the successful"; and on the eighth: "You have become secure, you will not fear"; and on the ninth, written: "You have been made companions of the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs"; and on the tenth, written: "You have dwelt in the neighbourhood of One who does not harm neighbours." Then the angels say: "Enter it in peace, secure."

"When they entered houses raised up, they said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has removed grief from us...' to His saying: 'fatigue.'"

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 35, verse 15–35 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. That is not difficult for Allah.﴾ ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl was asked about reconciling this verse with the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 13]. He said: ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ refers to bearing it willingly, while ﴿they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ refers to bearing it unwillingly.

﴿And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative﴾, meaning: if a soul burdened with the sins of others calls [someone] to carry its load, that is, the load of the sins upon it, nothing of it will be carried, even if the one called were a relative: his son, his mother, his father, or his brother.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Razmah al-Qazwini narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abd ibn Amir al-Samarqandi, who said: Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Fudayl ibn Iyad say regarding the words of the Exalted, ﴿nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative﴾: The mother will meet her son on the Day of Resurrection and say: "My son, did not my belly serve as a vessel for you? Did not my breast provide you with drink?" He will say: "Yes, O mother." She will say: "My son, my sins have weighed me down, so carry one sin of mine for me." He will say: "O mother, leave me alone, for today I am preoccupied with myself."

﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, that is, who fear Him though they have not seen Him, ﴿and establish the prayer. Whoever purifies himself, purifies only for his own soul. And to Allah is the final return.﴾ "Purifies himself" means one who does good and righteous deeds. 

﴿The blind and the seeing are not alike﴾, meaning: the ignorant and the knowledgeable; ﴿nor are darknesses and light﴾, meaning: disbelief and faith; ﴿nor shade and scorching heat﴾, meaning: Paradise and Hellfire. Al-harur is the hot wind by night and the simoom by day. Some said: al-harur is the heat with the sun during the day. ﴿Nor are the living and the dead alike﴾, meaning: the believers and the disbelievers. ﴿Indeed Allah causes to hear whom He wills﴾, until he takes admonition and responds, ﴿but you cannot make hear those in the graves﴾, meaning: the disbelievers, whom He likened to the dead. Ashhab al-Uqayli recited (bi-musmi'i man fi al-qubur) without tanwin, as an idafah (construct).

﴿You are only a warner. Indeed We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them. And if they deny you, those before them had denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs and written scriptures and the illuminating Book.﴾ He repeated them, though they are one thing, because the wordings differ.

﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My rejection!﴾

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors?﴾ The adjective was placed before the noun, and therefore it is in the accusative. ﴿And among the mountains are tracts, white and red, of varying shades, and extremely black.﴾ Judad means paths; its singular is jaddah, like mudda and mudad. The plural of jadid is judud (with a damma on the dal), like sarir and surar. Al-Farra' said: there is inversion in it; its meaning is "black ghiraab," and ghirabib is the plural of gharib, meaning intensely black, likened to the color of a crow. A poet, describing a vineyard, said:

Among the wonders of Allah's creation is a vine-clustered one, some of its grapes greenish and others ghirabib.

﴿And among people, beasts, and livestock, their colors vary likewise.﴾ The historian said: the pronoun "alwanuhu" (its colors) is because of "min" (among). Ustadhi Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ayyash say: He said "alwanuhu" because it refers back to "ma" in the implied sense, meaning: among people, beasts, and livestock is that whose colors vary.

﴿Thus﴾: the sentence is complete here, meaning: among these things are those whose colors vary according to the variation of fruits. Then He began, saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.﴾ It is narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he recited (innama yakhsha Allahu) with Allah in the nominative and (al-'ulama') in the accusative, which was the choice of Abu Hanifa, meaning "Allah knows," and it was said: "chooses." The correct reading is that of the common people.

It was also said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us from Ishaq ibn Sadaqah, who said: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us from Sayf ibn Umar, who said: Abbas ibn Awsajah narrated to us from Ata' al-Khurasani, raising the hadith, who said: Fear appeared in Abu Bakr to the point that it was recognized in him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) spoke to him about that, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah﴾ concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him). And in the hadith: "The most knowledgeable of them of Allah is the one most fearful of Him."

Masruq said: It is sufficient knowledge for a person that he fears Allah, and sufficient ignorance for a person that he is pleased with his knowledge.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Rabi'i narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Muharrami narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Malik al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'd narrated to us from Salih ibn Muslim al-Laythi, who said: A man came to al-Sha'bi and said: "Give me a fatwa, O scholar!" He said: "The scholar is one who fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty, Forgiving. Indeed those who recite the Book of Allah...﴾ The verse. Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: This is the verse of the reciters: ﴿and establish the prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: Ju'aywah narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr al-Laythi that he said: A man stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is it that I do not love death?" He said: "Do you have wealth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then send it forward." He said: "I cannot." He said: "Indeed, the heart of a person is with his wealth: if he sends it forward, he loves to be joined to it, and if he delays it, he loves to be delayed along with it."

﴿Hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾. Al-Farra' said: the phrase "yarjuna" (hoping) is the response to "inna alladhina yatlun" (indeed those who recite).

﴿That He may give them their full rewards and increase them from His bounty. Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it. Indeed Allah is, of His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing.﴾ "Thumma" is related back to what precedes it of the books of Allah in His words "limа bayna yadayhi" (what is before it), meaning the earlier books that preceded it; that is, We sent down those books. ﴿Then We caused to inherit this Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants.﴾ It is possible that "thumma" here means "wa" (and), meaning "and We caused to inherit," like His words: ﴿and then he was among those who believed﴾ [Surah al-Balad: 17], meaning "and he was." The meaning of "awrathna" is "We gave," because inheritance is a gift; this was said by Mujahid. Some of the people of meaning said: "awrathna" means "We delayed," and from it comes "mirath" (inheritance), because it comes after the deceased. Its meaning: We delayed the Qur'an relative to the earlier nations, and We gave it to you and qualified you for it. Antarah said:

And I bequeathed my sword from Husayn ibn Mu'aqqil, to his grandfather; indeed I am seeking my vengeance.

That is, I delayed it. In this is an honour for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), since He said "awrathna" to them, and said to the other nations: ﴿inherit the Book﴾, the verse, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He divided them into three classes and ranked them into three degrees, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾. He restricted the word and attached the wronging to the self, and therefore it is permissible that he be among those chosen despite his wronging.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in mentioning the wrongdoer first and delaying the foremost, when one normally mentions the more excellent first?

The answer to that is that we say: He delayed the foremost so that he would be nearer to the gardens and the reward, just as He mentioned the monasteries, churches and prayers in Surat al-Hajj before the mosques, which are the most excellent places on earth, so that the monasteries would be nearer to destruction and ruin, and the mosques nearer to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.

Some said: this was done because when kings wish to combine things in mention, they put the lesser before the greater, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 6], and He said: ﴿He causes the night to enter the day﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 61], and He said: ﴿He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 49], and He said: ﴿He who created death and life﴾ [Surah al-Mulk: 2].

It was also said: He put the wrongdoer first so that he would not despair of His mercy, and delayed the foremost so that he would not be conceited about his deed.

Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "He began with the wrongdoer to inform that one draws near to Him only through the turning of His mercy and generosity, and that wronging does not affect the state of being chosen. Then He followed with the moderate, because they are between fear and hope, then He concluded with the foremost, so that no one would feel safe from the plotting of Allah, and they are all in Paradise by the sanctity of the word of sincerity."

Some of them said: He put the wrongdoer first because he had nothing to rely upon except the mercy of Allah, so he relied upon Allah and depended upon His mercy; the moderate relied upon his good opinion of his Lord; and the foremost relied upon his good deeds and obedience.

Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them in being chosen to remove objections regarding the bestowal, because being chosen necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitating being chosen. Therefore it was said: "Establish the lineage correctly, then hope for the inheritance."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He arranged them in this order according to the stations of people, because the states of a servant are three: disobedience, heedlessness, then repentance and nearness. When he disobeys, he enters the domain of the wrongdoers; when he repents, he enters the group of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are abundant, he is connected to Allah and enters the ranks of the foremost.

The exegetes and interpreters differed about the meaning of the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost, and they went on at length. I will mention the texts of what they said, and success is from Allah:

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Burhan ibn Ali al-Sufi and al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab informed me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us from al-A'mash from Abu Thabit that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my strangeness, comfort my loneliness, and grant me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, I am happier with that than you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah,﴾ and he said:

"As for the foremost, he will enter Paradise without reckoning. As for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be held in the place of standing, then he will enter Paradise. They are the ones who said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Kindi and al-A'mash said from a man from Abu Thabit. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qatee'i informed me from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal: my father narrated to me from Ishaq ibn Isa, who narrated to me from Anas ibn Iyad al-Laythi Abu Damrah, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Azdi, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah.﴾ As for those who were foremost in good deeds, they are those who enter Paradise without reckoning. As for those who were moderate, they will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they are the ones who will be kept long in the place of gathering; then they are the ones whom Allah receives with His mercy, and they are the ones who say: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief...﴾ to His words: ﴿weariness﴾."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Sam'an al-Dharrar narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri' at Wasit narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: Faraj ibn Fudalah narrated to us from Azhar ibn Abd Allah al-Harrazi, who said: One who heard Uthman ibn Affan narrated to me that he recited this verse: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants,﴾ the verse, and said: "Our foremost are the people of our jihad, our moderate are the people of our settled regions, and our wrongdoers are the people of our desert."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us from al-Salt ibn Dinar, saying: Uqbah ibn Sahban narrated to us, saying: I entered upon Aisha and asked her about the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; among them is one who wrongs himself...﴾ She said to me: "My son, they are all in Paradise. As for the foremost in good deeds, they are those who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bore witness of Paradise. As for the moderate, they are those who followed his path among his companions until they joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and you." Thus she placed herself with us.

Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: they said they are the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah) ... ; ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾: they are the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah) ...; ﴿and among them is one foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾: they are the foremost, the drawn near (al-muqarrabun), among all people.

Qatadah said: This is in the world, in three stations; and at death Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And as for if he was of the companions of the right... and the burning of Hell﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 90–94], and in the Hereafter also, He the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And you will be three groups. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right! ... the drawn near﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 7–11].

Ibn Abbas said: The foremost is the sincere believer, the moderate is the showy one, and the wrongdoer is the one ungrateful for the blessings of Allah, though not denying them, because He judged for all three the entry into Paradise, saying: ﴿gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾. I heard Abu Muhammad Shaybah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abd say: Aisha said:

The foremost: the one who embraced Islam before the Hijrah; the moderate: the one who embraced Islam after the Hijrah; and the wrongdoer: we.

Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati said: The one who wrongs himself is the one who died upon a major sin without repenting from it; the moderate is the one who did not commit a major sin; and the foremost in good deeds is the one who never disobeyed Allah, and the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.

From al-Hasan also, he said: The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds; the moderate is the one whose good and evil deeds are equal; and the wrongdoer is the one whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: The foremost is the scholar, the moderate is the student, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant. And from him also: The foremost is the one occupied with his afterlife; the moderate is the one occupied with his afterlife rather than his livelihood; and the wrongdoer is the one occupied with his livelihood rather than his afterlife.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the seeker of this world, the moderate is the seeker of the final abode, and the foremost is the seeker of the Lord.

It was said: The wrongdoer is the Muslim, the moderate is the believer, and the foremost is the doer of good.

And they said: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: ... (no, continue below)

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given. Here is the translation:

And it was said: "The wrongdoer (al-zalim) is the one who shows off (yura'i) in all his deeds; the moderate (al-muqtasid) is the one whose deeds are partly for show and partly sincere; and the foremost (al-sabiq) is the one who is sincere in all his deeds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who takes the world, whether lawful or unlawful; the moderate is the one who strives to seek what is lawful; and the foremost is the one who has abandoned the world entirely and turned away from it."

Abu 'Uthman al-Hiri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who knows Allah with his tongue but whose deeds do not agree with his words; the moderate is the one who knows Him with his tongue and obeys Him with his limbs; and the foremost is the one who knows Him with his tongue, obeys Him with his limbs, and is sincere in his work." It was also said: "The foremost are the first emigrants (al-muhajirun al-awwalun), the moderate are the general body of the Companions, and the wrongdoers are the Successors (al-tabi'un)."

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz in Egypt say: Ibn 'Ata said: "The wrongdoer is the one whom you love for the sake of this world; the moderate is the one whom you love for the sake of the Hereafter; and the foremost is the one who lets his own desire fall before the desire of the Truth, so he sees no seeking or wanting for himself, because the authority of the Truth has overwhelmed him." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one whose outward appearance is better than his inward; the moderate is the one whose outward and inward are equal; and the foremost is the one whose inward is better than his outward."

It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Allah out of fear of the Fire; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of hope for Paradise; and the foremost is the one who worships Him without any cause." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the ascetic (al-zahid), the moderate is the knower (al-'arif), and the foremost is the lover (al-muhibb)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who despairs at affliction; the moderate is the one who is patient at affliction; and the foremost is the one who delights in affliction." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who worships Him out of heedlessness and habit; the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and dread; and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe and sight of the favour." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is given and then withholds; the moderate is the one who is given and then gives; and the foremost is the one who is withheld from and then gives thanks." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the heedless; the moderate is the seeker; and the foremost is the one who finds." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who is self-sufficient through his wealth; the moderate is the one who is self-sufficient through his religion; and the foremost is the one who is self-sufficient through his Lord." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the reciter of the Qur'an; the moderate is the reciter and the scholar of it; and the foremost is the reciter of the Book of Allah, the scholar of the Book of Allah, and the one who acts upon it." It was also said: "The foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the call to prayer (adhan); the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the adhan has been called; and the wrongdoer is the one who enters the mosque after the iqamah has been given." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is the one who loves himself; the moderate is the one who loves his Lord; and the foremost is the one whom his Lord loves." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who seeks; the moderate is one who is sought; and the foremost is one who is brought near (maqrub)." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is one who is called; the moderate is one who is given permission; and the foremost is one who is brought near." It was also said: "The wrongdoer is 'afuf; the moderate is alluf; and the foremost is halif."

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: "The wrongdoer seeks justice but does not grant it; the moderate grants justice and seeks it; and the foremost grants justice but does not seek it."

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "The wrongdoer is the one who does not mention Allah with his tongue; the moderate is the one who mentions Him with his heart; and the foremost is the one who does not forget his Lord."
